source.name: Desuarchive + RBT database dumps (2019-09)
source.short-desc: Dumps from the Desuarchive and RBT databases, made around September 20th 2019
source.capture:
23 per-board mysqldumps as .sql.bz2, 45GB total, and NOTHING ELSE — no image or thumbnail payloads anywhere in the item, so no download.exclude is needed. Surveyed against archive.org/metadata (27 files, 23 of them board dumps, the rest IA bookkeeping).

BOARDS: a (9.4GB), int (5.5), tg (4.8), co (3.9), g (3.5), r9k (3.3), mu (3.2), mlp (2.2), fit (2.2), k (1.9), trash (1.6), m (910MB), his (537), vr (373), gif (349), cgl (322), d (282), aco (208), qa (160), wsg (139), c (108), an (84), q (58).

WHY THIS ITEM MATTERS: it is the only source in the registry carrying /g/ and /r9k/ at this date. /g/ currently stops dead after 2017 and /r9k/ is 97% a single year (2015, from laza), so a 2019-09 Desuarchive dump is the first thing that reaches into either gap. Do not judge its value by compressed size — bz2 on post text is very dense.

TWO WARNINGS FROM THE UPLOADER'S OWN DESCRIPTION, both of which must be verified before a run is trusted:
1. The dumps were made with `mysqlchump`, described by the uploader as 'an experimental tool to make .sql dumps without needing to include all columns from the DB' and 'They probably work, but haven't been tested.' A dump missing columns is exactly the failure mode the adapters cannot see: fuuka-sql recognises a board table by requiring num, subnum, thread_num, timestamp, comment, and if a column is absent it SILENTLY ACCEPTS ZERO TABLES and ingests nothing rather than erroring. Check the CREATE TABLE and the accepted-table list, never a clean exit code.
2. 'These dumps will not configure the asagi triggers and procedures; if you want the _images tables etc., you will need to run asagi against your DB, then import.' Irrelevant here — this store only reads board tables and skips side tables — but it confirms the dumps are partial by design.

ADAPTER: desuarchive-sql, written for this dialect and verified against a slice of g.sql.bz2 read while it was still downloading (bzip2 decompresses from the start, so the schema is answerable before a 45GB fetch completes).

The SCHEMA is ordinary Asagi — num, subnum, thread_num, op, timestamp, comment, all present, engine TokuDB. But the SERIALIZATION is mysqlchump's and breaks fuuka-sql in three separate ways: `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`; an explicit INSERT column list that omits doc_id/media_id/poster_ip; and, worst, statements that span many lines because comments carry LITERAL UNESCAPED NEWLINES. There is also a UTF-8 BOM before each table's first INSERT, and values are separated by `, ` rather than `,`.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: timestamps are America/New_York wall time and get nyWallToUtc, confirmed by diffing 2,500 posts shared with installgentoo — exactly 5h behind stored UTC in Nov 2011/Jan 2012, exactly 4h in Jun 2017, i.e. tracking EST/EDT.

Throughput on a 297MB slice: 1,008,461 posts in 57s at 810MB peak RSS.

What this cost, recorded so nobody repeats it: pointed at these dumps, fuuka-sql reported `0 posts from tables []` and exited 0. After a partial fix it reported `0 posts from tables [g]` — a table accepted and yielding nothing, which reads exactly like a legitimate all-duplicates result. Never judge a run against this source by exit code; check the post count.
